condition: in vivo chronic low back pain

source.authors: Ng JK-F, Richardson CA, Parnianpour M, Kippers V
source.sample: right-handed male chronic/recurrent LBP patients, pain-free or minimal pain at testing; LBP duration 6.0±4.4 yr

title: Maximal isometric trunk moments in 6 directions, standing (B200 Isostation), chronic LBP patients

quantity.name: primary moment at MVC
quantity.definition: mean maximal isometric torque (stable 3 s of 5-s MVC) about dynamometer axes

protocol.summary: Erect standing in a B200 Isostation triaxial dynamometer locked in 3 planes, L5-S1 interspinous space aligned with its flexion/extension axis; pelvis and lower legs stabilised (pelvic restraint, thigh and knee straps); torso fixed by chest restraint and thoracic pad; arms folded across chest. MVCs (5 s, randomised, 2 min rest) in flexion, extension, R/L lateral flexion, R/L axial rotation with visual feedback and verbal encouragement; then R/L axial rotation at 70, 50, 30% MVC to a visual target. Mean of stable 3 s; baseline (relaxed standing in device) subtracted. Same lab/protocol as Ng 2001.
how_to_simulate: Upright standing, pelvis and legs fixed, thorax restrained by chest pad
Maximal voluntary exertion in flexion, extension, R/L lateral bending, R/L axial rotation
Compare predicted maximal primary moment at L5-S1 with mean ± SD
protocol.notes: Reference: B200 axes, flexion/extension axis at L5-S1 interspinous space. No significant strength difference patients vs controls. Coupled moments during the flexion/extension/lateral MVCs not reported.

extraction.uncertainty: ±3 Nm (bar chart, 0.93 px/Nm at 200 dpi, ticks every 50 Nm)
extraction.check_notes: Pixel digitisation of bar tops and one-sided SD caps (200 dpi); re-digitised at 300 dpi: control extension 180.7/27.1 vs 180.4/27.8, patient flexion cap 150.7 vs 150.4 Nm.
